mcat_description.short: Greenhouse Design Services covers end-to-end design, engineering, and construction of agricultural greenhouse and polyhouse structures in India, delivered as a turnkey or consultancy service. Providers design structures using GI pipe frameworks with polyethylene film, polycarbonate sheet, or shade net cladding, tailored to the buyer's crop, land area, and agro-climatic zone.
mcat_description.long: Greenhouse Design Services in India encompasses site assessment, structural engineering, material procurement, and on-site construction of protected cultivation structures — primarily polyhouses, shade net houses, and climate-controlled greenhouses — for commercial horticulture and floriculture. Service providers design structures compliant with BIS standards (IS 14462:1997, IS 14485:1998) and National Horticulture Board (NHB) norms, which mandate hot-dip galvanized pipe frameworks and UV-stabilized cladding films to qualify for government subsidy. The service spans multiple structure types — naturally ventilated polyhouses, fan-and-pad climate-controlled greenhouses, polycarbonate greenhouses, shade net houses, and walk-in tunnels — each suited to different agro-climatic zones, crops, and investment levels. Buyers typically engage service providers for a complete turnkey project from DPR preparation and subsidy documentation through structural erection, irrigation integration, and crop commissioning.

market_context: In India, 'Greenhouse Design Services' is commercially synonymous with polyhouse design and construction services — polyhouse (polyethylene-covered) being the dominant technology due to lower cost and wide availability. The market is structured around turnkey project delivery, where a single contractor handles site assessment, structural design, material supply, erection, and irrigation integration. NHB (National Horticulture Board) and state horticulture department subsidies are a major demand driver, making NHB compliance (hot-dip galvanized GI pipe, minimum 300 GSM; UV-stabilized 200-micron film) a critical buyer requirement. BIS standards IS 14462:1997 (layout and design recommendations) and IS 14485:1998 (heating, ventilating, and cooling) govern structural design, alongside IS 875 (1987) for load calculations. Structural designs vary by agro-climatic zone — Quonset, gothic arch, saw-tooth, and multi-span designs are common — and a single design cannot be adopted across all regions due to varying wind speeds (33–55 m/s across India). Key service providers include Agriplast Protected Cultivation, InHydro, Parasnath Polyagro, GM Greenhouses (Pune), Vasupujya Tradelink (Ahmedabad), and Hindustan Agri Business. The market spans commercial farmers, floriculture exporters, agri-startups, and institutional buyers across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh as primary hubs.
